_source: Theatre-level archive-memory library. Seeded from public Criterion archive material at https://criteriontheatre.co.uk/archive/find/memory, already curated and provenance-checked in the Popcorn pack. All quotes are verbatim and attributed to their original authors. See content-snapshot.md for source URLs and approval dates.
_curation_principle: Warm, theatrical, credited stories that honour the volunteer ethos and read well at 5-6 metres in 10-13 seconds. No invented nostalgia, no uncredited quotations, no personal/private material. Kept deliberately small; add only after a provenance, attribution and sensitivity check.

memories.author: Karl Stafford
memories.quote: …In those days, money was tight and materials short… All nails were recovered and straightened… and the wooden beer crates were repurposed for all manner of uses on stage.

memories.author: Phil Reynolds
memories.quote: …On the opening night there was a severe snowstorm; Elliot had been… wearing his heavy Russian overcoat and fur hat, and made his first entrance into my Moscow flat covered in real snow!

memories.author: Terry Nicholls
memories.quote: Mr. Ruscoe decided to put ice water in the bottle he squirted down my trousers… I had my revenge for the final scene of the play. John had to play it completely immobilised in a hospital bed… I emptied a bottle of ice water onto the mattress.

memories.author: Nicole Firth
memories.quote: The wonderful Doug Griffiths had to recite a list of countries every night… never quite got them in the same order or indeed the same list. Brings a smile to my face remembering this one.

memories.author: Chris Firth
memories.quote: …I had bundled up my costume… Linda Holmes, doing wardrobe, was not very happy with this. 'Who do you think is going to be ironing this costume?' At the time I thought there was an ironing fairy. My mum, as it turned out.

memories.author: Marcus Pugh
memories.quote: My father played Sky Masterson… a ring box was needed for the proposal scene. 'I have a ring box,' I enthusiastically chirped… Ring boxes, I am sure, were not in short supply in Coventry.
